name: stonedog-howto
description: A how-to documentation surface for applications: markdown articles that describe themselves in frontmatter, section manifests, per-article tables of contents, search, and access control supplied by the host.
author: StoneDogCode L.L.C.
//exports: This package ships TypeScript SOURCE, not a bundled dist/, for the same reason stonedog-style does: the React layer is styled with Panda CSS, which extracts styles by statically parsing source at the CONSUMER's build. A pre-bundled dist would emit class names the consumer's Panda never generated a stylesheet for. Consumers transpile us (Next.js: `transpilePackages: ['stonedog-howto']`) and add our src to their panda `include` globs.
//files: The __tests__ exclusion is load-bearing, not tidiness. Consumers add `node_modules/stonedog-howto/src/**` to their Panda `include` globs, so anything shipped under src/ is statically parsed at THEIR build — and the tests import jest globals and render fixture markup. They also ship a test suite nobody can run to every consumer.

scripts.//test: Jest runs as ESM (see jest.config.cjs), which needs the VM modules flag.
scripts.gate: npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm run test

//peerDependencies: react/react-dom are peers ONLY. Listing them as dependencies too makes npm install a second copy into this package, and two Reacts in one tree fail at runtime with 'Invalid hook call' — a failure that points at the consumer's component, not at this manifest.
